### References of the table

[1] Echo level chosen to reproduce the usual B-mode appearance of the tissue (ACR BI-RADS ultrasound lexicon; for breast masses see also Nam et al. 2013). A modelling choice, not a measurement.

[2] Culjat M.O., Goldenberg D., Tewari P., Singh R.S. A review of tissue substitutes for ultrasound imaging. Ultrasound Med. Biol. 36(6):861-873, 2010. doi:10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2010.02.012 (Table 1, values from ICRU Report 61, 1998)

[3] IT'IS Foundation. Tissue Properties Database V5.0, 21 August 2025. doi:10.13099/VIP21000-05-0 (average values; attenuation converted from Np/(m MHz^y) with 1 Np = 8.686 dB)

[4] Katz-Hanani I., Rothstein T., Gaitini D., Gallimidi Z., Azhari H. Age-related ultrasonic properties of breast tissue in vivo. Ultrasound Med. Biol. 40(9):2265-2271, 2014. doi:10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2014.03.034

[6] Keshavarzi A., Vaezy S., Kaczkowski P.J., et al. Attenuation coefficient and sound speed in human myometrium and uterine fibroid tumors. J. Ultrasound Med. 20(5):473-480, 2001. doi:10.7863/jum.2001.20.5.473

[8] Law W.K., Frizzell L.A., Dunn F. Determination of the nonlinearity parameter B/A of biological media. Ultrasound Med. Biol. 11(2):307-318, 1985. doi:10.1016/0301-5629(85)90130-9

[9] Li C., Duric N., Littrup P., Huang L. In vivo breast sound-speed imaging with ultrasound tomography. Ultrasound Med. Biol. 35(10):1615-1628, 2009. doi:10.1016/j.ultrasmedbio.2009.05.011

`*` modelling choice where no measurement fits; the notes below give the reason.

### Notes on each value

**fat**: c: breast fat in vivo, ultrasound tomography, 61 women; used for all adipose layers; rho: fat, 23 samples; alpha0: breast fat in vivo, slope at 7 MHz, 24 women; y: linear frequency dependence assumed for the slope; ba: fat: B/A around 11; k: fat; cp: fat; perfusion: fat; echo: reference level; breast fat is the BI-RADS standard of comparison.

**muscle**: c: skeletal muscle, mean of 24 values; rho: skeletal muscle, 14 samples; alpha0: 7.11 Np/(m MHz^y); ba: muscle: B/A close to 7; perfusion: resting muscle; echo: muscle is hypoechoic to fat.

**water**: c: water at 37 C; rho: water at 37 C; alpha0: 0.0253 Np/(m MHz) at 1 MHz; y: viscous absorption grows with f^2; IT'IS lists a linear law, which understates the loss above 1 MHz; ba: room temperature; echo: anechoic.

**blood**: rho: 584 samples; alpha0: 2.37 Np/(m MHz^y); perfusion: flowing blood in a vessel; heat carried by flow is not a Pennes term; echo: nearly anechoic at clinical frequencies.

**epidermis**: c: excised skin, 20-30 MHz, 24 C; rho: skin; alpha0: fit alpha1 f^n over 20-30 MHz; y: fit over 20-30 MHz; ba: soft tissue value; k: skin; cp: skin; perfusion: the epidermis has no blood vessels; echo: bright entry echo.

**dermis**: c: excised skin, 20-30 MHz, 24 C; rho: skin; alpha0: fit alpha1 f^n over 20-30 MHz; y: fit over 20-30 MHz; ba: soft tissue value; k: skin; cp: skin; perfusion: skin; echo: dermis is hyperechoic to subcutaneous fat.

**smas**: superficial musculoaponeurotic system, given the acoustic and thermal properties of dermis (dense connective tissue); no direct measurement; c: excised skin, 20-30 MHz, 24 C; value of dermis; rho: skin; value of dermis; alpha0: fit alpha1 f^n over 20-30 MHz; value of dermis; y: fit over 20-30 MHz; value of dermis; ba: soft tissue value; value of dermis; k: skin; value of dermis; cp: skin; value of dermis; perfusion: skin; value of dermis; echo: fibrous layer, echogenic band in the subcutis.

**fibroglandular tissue**: c: breast parenchyma in vivo, ultrasound tomography; rho: breast; alpha0: breast; whole breasts in vivo range from 0.96 (over 60 years) to 1.27 (under 30) dB/(cm MHz), Katz-Hanani et al. 2014; y: slope in dB/(cm MHz); ba: soft tissue value; k: breast gland; cp: breast gland; perfusion: breast gland; echo: fibroglandular tissue is hyperechoic to fat.

**cooper ligament**: connective tissue band, given the properties of dermis; c: excised skin, 20-30 MHz, 24 C; value of dermis; rho: skin; value of dermis; alpha0: fit alpha1 f^n over 20-30 MHz; value of dermis; y: fit over 20-30 MHz; value of dermis; ba: soft tissue value; value of dermis; k: skin; value of dermis; cp: skin; value of dermis; perfusion: skin; value of dermis; echo: thin echogenic septa.

**breast cyst**: simple cyst fluid modelled as water at 37 C; c: water at 37 C; value of water; rho: water at 37 C; value of water; alpha0: 0.0253 Np/(m MHz) at 1 MHz; value of water; y: viscous absorption grows with f^2; IT'IS lists a linear law, which understates the loss above 1 MHz; value of water; ba: room temperature; value of water; k: value of water; cp: value of water; perfusion: value of water; echo: simple cyst: anechoic.

**fibroadenoma**: c: benign breast lesions in vivo, mean of the cohort; rho: breast gland; alpha0: 14 fibroadenomas in vivo, reference phantom method; y: slope in dB/(cm MHz); ba: soft tissue value; k: breast gland; cp: breast gland; perfusion: breast gland; echo: oval circumscribed mass, mildly hypoechoic to fat.

**breast carcinoma**: c: malignant breast lesions in vivo, mean of the cohort; rho: breast gland; alpha0: 10 carcinomas in vivo, reference phantom method; y: slope in dB/(cm MHz); ba: soft tissue value; k: human breast adenocarcinoma, 37 C; cp: middle of the 3.6-3.9 J/(g K) range of malignant tumours; perfusion: breast gland; echo: hypoechoic mass; most carcinomas have a lower backscatter than fibroadenomas (Nam et al. 2013).

**prostate**: c: from Parker et al. 1993; with rho gives 1.63 MRayl; rho: same value in IT'IS; alpha0: value used for prostate tissue in their simulations; y: exponent used with alpha0; k: IT'IS gives 0.512; cp: freshly excised prostate (Patch et al. 2011); perfusion: normal prostate; echo: peripheral zone: homogeneous, isoechoic, darker than periprostatic fat.

**prostate transition zone**: c: from Parker et al. 1993; with rho gives 1.63 MRayl; value of prostate; rho: same value in IT'IS; value of prostate; alpha0: value used for prostate tissue in their simulations; value of prostate; y: exponent used with alpha0; value of prostate; ba: value of prostate; k: IT'IS gives 0.512; value of prostate; cp: freshly excised prostate (Patch et al. 2011); value of prostate; perfusion: normal prostate; value of prostate; echo: transition zone: hypoechoic and heterogeneous with age.

**prostate carcinoma**: acoustic and thermal properties of normal prostate, with the lower perfusion measured in carcinoma; no measured in vivo acoustic values; c: from Parker et al. 1993; with rho gives 1.63 MRayl; value of prostate; rho: same value in IT'IS; value of prostate; alpha0: value used for prostate tissue in their simulations; value of prostate; y: exponent used with alpha0; value of prostate; ba: value of prostate; k: IT'IS gives 0.512; value of prostate; cp: freshly excised prostate (Patch et al. 2011); value of prostate; perfusion: 1.7 kg/(m^3 s), measured in patients with locally advanced carcinoma (van Vulpen et al. 2002); echo: classically hypoechoic in the peripheral zone.

**calcification**: c: renal stones (Singh and Agarwal 1989); with rho gives 3.20 MRayl; rho: renal stones; alpha0: value used for prostatic calcifications; y: exponent used with alpha0; k: calcium carbonate; cp: calcium carbonate; echo: bright echo with acoustic shadow.

**rectal wall**: given the properties of muscle; c: skeletal muscle, mean of 24 values; value of muscle; rho: skeletal muscle, 14 samples; value of muscle; alpha0: 7.11 Np/(m MHz^y); value of muscle; y: value of muscle; ba: muscle: B/A close to 7; value of muscle; k: value of muscle; cp: value of muscle; perfusion: resting muscle; value of muscle; echo: layered muscular wall.

**bladder wall**: given the properties of muscle; c: skeletal muscle, mean of 24 values; value of muscle; rho: skeletal muscle, 14 samples; value of muscle; alpha0: 7.11 Np/(m MHz^y); value of muscle; y: value of muscle; ba: muscle: B/A close to 7; value of muscle; k: value of muscle; cp: value of muscle; perfusion: resting muscle; value of muscle; echo: thin echogenic wall.

**urine**: modelled as water at 37 C; c: water at 37 C; value of water; rho: water at 37 C; value of water; alpha0: 0.0253 Np/(m MHz) at 1 MHz; value of water; y: viscous absorption grows with f^2; IT'IS lists a linear law, which understates the loss above 1 MHz; value of water; ba: room temperature; value of water; k: value of water; cp: value of water; perfusion: value of water; echo: anechoic.

**myometrium**: c: fresh ex vivo, 1-3 MHz: 1611-1616 m/s for myometrium and fibroid; rho: uterus; alpha0: power law through the 5 and 10 MHz values of the abstract (4.15 and 12.6 dB/cm); y: same fit; ba: soft tissue value; k: uterus; cp: uterus; perfusion: uterus; echo: homogeneous, intermediate echo level.

**fibroid**: c: fresh ex vivo, 1-3 MHz; rho: uterus; alpha0: leiomyoma: power law through 5.1 and 16.0 dB/cm at 5 and 10 MHz; y: same fit; ba: soft tissue value; k: uterus; cp: uterus; perfusion: fibroids chosen for HIFU are usually hypovascular, so a value well below that of myometrium; perfusion varies widely between fibroids; echo: usually hypoechoic whorled mass.

**cervix**: c: cervix; rho: cervix; alpha0: power law through 6.3 and 26.8 dB/cm at 5 and 10 MHz; y: same fit; ba: soft tissue value; k: cervix; cp: cervix; perfusion: cervix; echo: intermediate echo level.

**endometrium**: acoustic and thermal properties of myometrium; c: fresh ex vivo, 1-3 MHz: 1611-1616 m/s for myometrium and fibroid; value of myometrium; rho: uterus; value of myometrium; alpha0: power law through the 5 and 10 MHz values of the abstract (4.15 and 12.6 dB/cm); value of myometrium; y: same fit; value of myometrium; ba: soft tissue value; value of myometrium; k: uterus; value of myometrium; cp: uterus; value of myometrium; perfusion: uterus; value of myometrium; echo: echogenic stripe (secretory phase).

**bone**: fluid model: shear waves are not included; c: cortical bone, compressional wave; rho: cortical bone, 27 samples; alpha0: cortical bone, 54.6 Np/(m MHz); ba: no measurement; enters only through the nonlinear term; k: cortical bone; cp: cortical bone; perfusion: cortical bone; echo: bright surface with shadow.
